thread:
maria: quick sync — i want to land a small followup from the continuous-batcher RFC: tighten the scheduler <-> queueing boundary so adapters can implement prefetch/backpressure without pulling scheduler internals. thoughts?

alex: +1. current coupling makes it hard to reason about admission. i hit it when adding tenant headroom metrics.

kyle: can you sketch the new surface? curious how much logic we move to adapters vs keep in scheduler.

maria: idea: scheduler owns coarse admission (credits, deadlines, lane assignment). adapters own local shaping, prefetch, and KV warmup hints. contract is a tiny token handshake: request -> scheduler returns {lease_id, deadline_ms, credit_cost, warmup_hint}. adapter can `reserve(lease_id)` and `release(lease_id)` when it materializes a microbatch.

alex: that sounds doable. few constraints: 1) scheduler must be able to revoke leases quickly for preemption, 2) adapters need lightweight signal for warmup cancelation.

kyle: for revocation, we should avoid blocking RPCs. suggest ephemeral revocation channel in the runtime (pubsub) and a best-effort callback inside adapter. if adapter misses revoke, scheduler will mark lease stale and ignore it on dispatch.

maria: agree. here's a tiny proto sketch i threw together:

```
message Lease {
  string id = 1;
  uint64 deadline_ms = 2;
  uint32 credit = 3;
  string warmup_hint = 4; // opaque to scheduler
}

rpc AcquireLease(AcquireRequest) returns (Lease);
rpc ReleaseLease(ReleaseRequest) returns (Empty);
// revocations stream from scheduler -> adapter: Revoked(lease_id)
```

diane: i like the separation. one question: how do we reason about latency SLOs w/ adapter-local shaping? adapter could buffer too long. need a guardrail.

maria: two guardrails: 1) scheduler deadline_ms is authoritative; any adapter-held microbatch must honor it (adapter drops or converts to fastpath). 2) add per-lease telemetry: queued_ms, warmup_ms, dispatch_ms. alert on queued_ms > X% of deadline.

tim: for rollout, we should keep both modes: old tightly-coupled behavior and new contract. feature-flag the adapter-facing API and run canary on a subset of hosts.

alex: migration checklist:
- implement Acquire/Release in new adapter shim
- expose revocation stream (kafka/pubsub) + library helpers
- add metrics and SLO-based alerting
- enable flag for 10% traffic, measure tail latency and cost
- iterate

kyle: question on admission accounting: if adapter prefetches keys and consumes credits, how do we avoid double-charging when scheduler later packs with other requests?

maria: treat adapter prefetch as provisional credit usage. scheduler final accounting happens on dispatch. if adapter prefetches but request gets cancelled, adapter releases provisional credit back to scheduler. keep provisionally charged credits in a cheap in-memory ledger.

diane: sounds complex but doable. we should add TTL on provisional credits to avoid leaks if adapter crashes. also an async reconciler job.

infra-bot: NOTE: created issue #INF-2484 "adapter lease API + revocation stream" (link: https://redwood/INF-2484)

tim: small perf thought — keep lease objects very small (ids + deadline); warmup_hint can be a token referencing a separate hotstore. avoids blowing RPC size when adapters send big hints.

alex: +1. also add a compact lease protobuf and an opt-in verbose lease for debugging.

maria: final asks for implementers: keep the handshake simple, instrument provisional vs final credit flows, TTLs on provisional credits, and a safe fallback mode that maps old behavior to the new API. i'll draft an RFC addendum with diagrams.

kyle: thanks — will prototype adapter shim this week. will post perf numbers.

diane: pls include a test plan for failure modes (adapter crash, revocation lost, scheduler restart). those behaved oddly in prior rollouts.

maria: noted. test plan + rollout strategy in RFC addendum. thanks all :rocket:

tim: ping @maria when draft is up, happy to help review rollout playbook.

maria: will do. closing the sync — followup in INF-2484 and RFC addendum.
